title: Legacy quiesce drill
description: Objective: preview, authorize, prove, and rehearse GO_QUIESCE over every legacy writer/process/access path, immutable snapshot, import, backup, and abort restoration. Deliverable: a non-production cutover drill with exact manifests. NOT in scope: activating v2. Hard dependencies: Deterministic legacy importer, Portability shadow gate, Disaster restore proof, and explicit human GO_QUIESCE. Owned paths: tests/migration/cutover/** and cutover evidence only. Verification: pnpm test:migration.
definitionOfDone: All known daemon, IDE, launcher, watcher, scheduled start, process, handle, and access paths are inventoried and stopped/denied.
Two complete manifests at least ten seconds apart match before import.
Abort restores pre-cutover access safely and legacy bytes remain readable/unchanged.
taskRails: Claims follow the benchmark permit-list; missing, partial, cross-basis, or unverifiable evidence is UNKNOWN, never PASS.
No confirmatory corpus is generated or viewed until the implementation commit is frozen exactly as specified.
GO_QUIESCE and GO_ACTIVATE are separate human decisions. Keep evidence exact, reproducible, and scoped to one source commit.

implementationPlan.description: SCOPE FENCE — read this before anything else. This task was audited and returned to BLOCKED because it carries an explicit human GO_QUIESCE gate that has never been given. The human was asked directly this session and answered "plan as much as u can prod way and try not to block" — they did NOT give GO_QUIESCE. Therefore: this plan builds the drill HARNESS and exercises it against an ISOLATED SANDBOX FIXTURE TREE created under the OS temp directory. It does NOT stop, deny, signal, kill or otherwise touch any real daemon, IDE, launcher, watcher, scheduled start, process or handle. That restriction is not a nicety — the moe daemon serving this board is itself one of the paths DoD 1 names, and three tasks are WORKING on it right now; a drill that stopped real paths would take the board down mid-flight. Any step below that seems to ask for a real path to be stopped is to be read as the fixture equivalent, and if you cannot see how to satisfy a DoD item against the fixture, report blocked rather than reaching for a real process. Baseline the lane: confirm `tests/migration/` currently contains only `import/import-determinism.test.ts`, confirm there is NO `tests/migration/tsconfig.json` and NO `test:migration` script in package.json (both measured absent this session), and capture the merge-base output of `pnpm test:migration` failing-because-absent so the step-8 comparison has a real baseline.

Make the lane real, because the task's own stated verification command does not exist. Create `tests/migration/tsconfig.json` mirroring `tests/security/tsconfig.json` exactly — `{"extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json", "compilerOptions": {"composite": false, "declaration": false, "declarationMap": false, "types": ["node"]}, "include": ["./**/*.ts"]}` — and create `tests/migration/vitest.config.ts` mirroring `tests/security/vitest.config.ts`. Then add to package.json scripts, following the exact convention the fault and security lanes already use: `"test:migration": "tsc -p tests/migration/tsconfig.json && vitest run --config tests/migration/vitest.config.ts"`. THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS TASK: there is no root tsconfig.json, `pnpm typecheck` is `pnpm --recursive typecheck` over workspace packages only, and `tests/migration/` has no tsconfig — so the existing `import-determinism.test.ts` and everything you are about to write are TYPECHECKED BY NOTHING until this step lands. Verify the new lane actually type-errors on a deliberate mistake before moving on, then remove the mistake; a tsconfig whose `include` misses the directory would leave the lane silently unchecked exactly as before. Note the root vitest.config.ts already includes `tests/**/*.test.ts` with `passWithNoTests: false`, so the new tests also run under plain `pnpm test` and an empty lane fails rather than passing.

Build the sandbox fixture: `tests/migration/cutover/cutover-fixture.ts` (target <=250 physical lines). It creates, under `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-cutover-"))`, a synthetic "legacy" tree with enough structure to be worth manifesting — nested directories, files of differing sizes, a zero-byte file, a file with non-ASCII bytes, a deeply nested path, and at least one file whose mtime is deliberately older than the others. Expose `createCutoverFixture()` returning the root plus a teardown, and `mutateOneByte(root)` which flips exactly one byte in exactly one named file and returns which — that mutator is the positive control step 5 depends on, so it must report what it changed rather than mutating silently. Also expose a simulated access-path table: a frozen list of named pseudo-processes/handles with an `open`/`deny` state that the inventory can read and flip, standing in for the real daemon/IDE/launcher/watcher paths WITHOUT touching any real one. Every path is built with `join`, never string concatenation, and teardown closes every handle BEFORE `rmSync` — on Windows an open handle makes the removal fail and leaves the temp tree behind. Nothing in this module reads a module under test or restates a cutover rule; a fixture that re-derived the manifest would let the suite agree with itself.

Build the manifest producer: `tests/migration/cutover/cutover-manifest.ts` (target <=250 lines). Export `captureCutoverManifest(root)` walking the tree deterministically — sorted by code-point order, never by directory-iteration order, which differs across platforms and would make two manifests of an unchanged tree disagree on macOS or Linux. Each entry binds the relative POSIX-normalised path, byte length, and a sha256 of the content; record the entry count explicitly so an empty or truncated walk cannot masquerade as a match. Export `compareCutoverManifests(a, b)` returning a structured result naming EVERY differing path with the kind of difference (ADDED, REMOVED, CONTENT_CHANGED, LENGTH_CHANGED) rather than a bare boolean — a boolean tells the operator nothing about what moved under them. Refuse and report, never throw, on an unreadable entry, and carry a stable reason code plus the failing path; an unreadable file must NEVER be silently skipped, because a skipped file is a file that could have changed unobserved. Bound the walk depth and entry count with explicit refusal codes rather than recursing without limit. Cross-platform: normalise separators for the manifest key but stat through the real path, and do not fold case — two files differing only in case are two files.

Build the inventory and abort halves: `tests/migration/cutover/cutover-inventory.ts` (target <=250 lines). Export `inventoryAccessPaths(table)` producing a frozen, deterministically ordered record of every declared access path with its state, and asserting the declared population is non-empty — an inventory over zero paths trivially reports "all stopped" and is the exact vacuity epic rail 6 warns about. Export `denyAccessPaths(table)` which flips every OPEN path to DENIED in the fixture table and returns the set it changed, and `restoreAccessPaths(table, saved)` which puts back exactly the saved states. Both operate ONLY on the fixture table from step 3 — there is no real-process code path in this module, and a comment must say so, because the next reader will otherwise assume a real one is missing. Every refusal carries a stable reason code and the layer that refused; a path that cannot be denied is reported by name and code, never assumed denied. `restoreAccessPaths` must be exact: restoring to "all open" rather than to the saved states would pass a naive test while destroying the very property DoD 3 asks about.

The drill itself: `tests/migration/cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts`. Compose the three modules into the four DoD checks, each with its vacuity guard. (1) INVENTORY — every declared access path is inventoried and ends DENIED; assert the inventoried count equals the declared count AND that the count is non-zero, then assert by NAME that each specific path is denied, not merely that a count matched. (2) TWO MANIFESTS TEN SECONDS APART — capture, wait a REAL >=10s measured from a monotonic clock, capture again, and assert they match. The test MUST assert the achieved elapsed gap was actually >=10_000ms; a faked or mocked timer, or a `setTimeout` whose delay was clamped, would make the whole assertion vacuous while it stayed green. Mark this test with an explicit timeout above the wait so vitest does not kill it mid-drill. (3) POSITIVE CONTROL, the assertion that makes (2) mean anything — run the same two-capture sequence but call `mutateOneByte` in between, and assert the comparison FAILS naming exactly the mutated path with CONTENT_CHANGED. Without this, a `compareCutoverManifests` that always returned "match" would pass (2) forever. (4) ABORT AND RESTORE — save states, deny everything, then abort: assert `restoreAccessPaths` returns every path to its exact saved state (not merely to open), and assert a manifest captured after the abort still matches the pre-cutover manifest byte for byte, proving the legacy bytes remained readable and unchanged throughout. Also assert the unreadable-entry and bound-exceeded refusals return their exact stable code and layer, never a bare throw.

Mutation drills, because three of the four DoD checks are the kind that pass while asserting nothing. Restore exact bytes from your own saved copy after each — never `git checkout`, which reverts to HEAD and destroys uncommitted work in this shared worktree. Drill A: make `compareCutoverManifests` always report a match. The POSITIVE CONTROL test from step 6 case 3 must go red; if it stays green, the comparison was never being exercised. Drill B: make `inventoryAccessPaths` return an empty population. The count assertion in case 1 must go red — this is the drill that proves the inventory is not vacuously satisfying "all paths stopped" over zero paths. Drill C: make `restoreAccessPaths` restore everything to OPEN instead of to the saved states. Case 4 must go red on the exact-state assertion; a test that only checked "restore ran" would survive this, so if it stays green the assertion is too weak and must be tightened rather than the drill abandoned. For each drill confirm it reddens for the RIGHT reason — not a crash inside a walker, not a timeout from the 10s wait, and not a broad over-reddening across the whole lane, which indicates a broken environment rather than a held guard. A guard with no operator to flip has no drill: if a body is a no-op, make it THROW to prove the call site is still on the path.

Verification and honest evidence. Run `pnpm test:migration` — the script this plan created in step 2, since it did not exist before — and capture its real exit code and output. Then run `pnpm test` so the root lane picks the new tests up via its `tests/**/*.test.ts` include, and confirm no other lane regressed. Use `&&` chaining, never `;` (a `;`-chained run reports exit 0 while a leg is red) and never pipe through tail (a piped run reports tail's exit code). Compare against the step-1 merge-base baseline; the HEAD-minus-baseline failing-path set intersected with this task's owned paths must be EMPTY, and any foreign red is reported verbatim with its exact failing lines and paths. Note the 10-second wait makes this lane genuinely slow — that is the drill working, not a hang; do not "optimise" it away with a fake clock. Then mechanically assert: every new source is <=250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (PowerShell Measure-Object -Line undercounts); the temp fixture directory is removed and no `moe-cutover-*` tree remains under the OS temp dir; and `git diff --check` plus `git status --porcelain` show no generated evidence file and no unowned staged path. Check whether tests/fault and tests/security carry `.js` bridges beside their `.ts` files and mirror whatever convention is actually there — do not assume either way.

Adversarial self-review, then record the scope honestly. Load `adversarial-self-review` and read the diff as an attacker: can the manifest walk skip an entry silently under any error; can two manifests of a CHANGED tree ever compare equal; is directory-iteration order leaking into the manifest so the same tree hashes differently on another OS; does the 10s wait actually elapse, or could a clamped timer or a vitest fake clock shorten it; does the inventory ever report success over an empty population; does abort restore to saved state rather than to a convenient default; do the bound and unreadable refusals carry exact codes and layers rather than throwing; and does anything in the diff reach a real process, socket, port, service handle or path outside the temp fixture — grep the diff for `kill`, `taskkill`, `exec`, `spawn`, `process.kill`, `net`, and any absolute path outside tmpdir, and confirm every hit is inside the fixture. THEN, before handoff, add a task comment stating plainly what this task DID and DID NOT deliver: the harness is built and drilled, and the LIVE quiesce against real daemon/IDE/launcher/watcher/scheduled-start paths was NOT performed and remains gated on explicit human GO_QUIESCE plus task-22cfca91 and task-0c89476b. Say that the narrowing was an explicit human instruction this session, not an architect's unilateral call. Stage and commit only `package.json`, `tests/migration/tsconfig.json`, `tests/migration/vitest.config.ts` and the four `tests/migration/cutover/` files by explicit pathspec — never `git add -A`, reset or stash. package.json is shared: stage only your `test:migration` hunk.

planningNotes.risks:
1. SAFETY, the dominant risk. DoD 1 names daemon, IDE, launcher, watcher and scheduled-start paths. The moe daemon serving this board IS one of them, and task-e33747f9, task-5dfc98fc and task-6f786c58 are WORKING on it. Nothing in this plan may stop, signal or kill a real process. Step 9 greps the diff for kill/taskkill/exec/spawn/process.kill/net and for any absolute path outside tmpdir precisely to catch a drift into that.
2. VACUITY is the second dominant risk and it is why three mutation drills are mandatory rather than optional. "All paths stopped" over an empty inventory passes. Two manifests compare equal if the comparator always says equal. "Abort restored" passes if restore just opens everything. Each has a named drill.
3. The ten-second rule must be REAL elapsed time from a monotonic clock, and the test must assert the achieved gap. A fake clock, a mocked timer, or a clamped setTimeout leaves DoD 2 green and meaningless. Give the test an explicit timeout above the wait so vitest does not kill it mid-drill.
4. Manifest determinism across OSes: sort by code point, never rely on directory iteration order; normalise separators for the key but stat the real path; never case-fold.
5. Windows fixture teardown: close every handle before rmSync or the temp tree leaks and the next run inherits it.
6. An unreadable file must refuse with a code, never be skipped — a skipped file is a file that could have changed unobserved, which is exactly what the drill exists to detect.
7. This task delivers a NARROWED scope by explicit human instruction. Step 9 requires that to be written onto the task in the worker's own words so a later reader never mistakes the harness for a completed live cutover, and so the GO_QUIESCE gate stays visibly open.
